title: Achieving Near-Zero Read Retry for 3D NAND Flash Memory
problem: As NAND flash memory ages with program/erase cycles, it requires increasing numbers of read retries for error correction, degrading read performance. Pre-defined read retry tables fail to account for read granularity and chip-specific error behaviors.
motivation: Optimizing read retry mechanisms is critical for maintaining flash read performance as storage devices age and error rates increase.
method: The paper characterizes different NAND flash chip types and error behaviors under aging, develops models for correlations among optimal read voltage offsets per page, generates tailored read retry tables (RRT) specific to each flash model, and proposes a dynamic read retry procedure that selects voltages from the table followed by proximity-search fine-tuning to minimize retries.
key_novelty: Generating chip-specific tailored read retry tables through characterization-driven modeling rather than using generic pre-defined retry tables embedded in flash controllers.
contributions: Characterization of real flash chip types and their error behaviors across aging cycles and retention time
Models for correlations among optimal read offsets required for different pages
Methodology to generate tailored read retry tables per flash model
Dynamic read retry procedure with proximity-search achieving near-zero retries

metrics.other: Average read retries reduced to below 0.003 at 8K P/E cycles versus 3+ retries at 3K P/E cycles with state-of-the-art

baselines: State-of-the-art pre-defined read retry table approaches
limitations: Paper does not discuss limitations in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: Adaptive read retry optimization for aged NAND flash
